summary: Tested the website tender-alert sign-up (double opt-in) and the weekly tender digest end to end. Backend: 15/15 new tests passed (tests/test_marketing_v59_signup_digest.py). The v58 marketing regression suite also passed (17/17). The digest logic was tested inside the backend process with send_email patched, so no real emails went out. It covers: category matching, the 15-tender cap, the 7-day window, contacts with no categories getting all tenders, skipping unsubscribed and non-consented contacts, the unsubscribe link, deduping runs in the same week, no scheduled run unless enabled and mode=weekly, and instant alerts being suppressed in weekly mode. Frontend: the homepage sign-up works. Submit stays disabled until both email and consent are filled, the signup-done message shows, and the contact is stored with pending country/category. On mobile (390px) the fields stack with no horizontal overflow. In the admin Alerts tab, the weekly/instant radios save and survive a reload, 'Send this week's digest now' shows a toast and a log row, and the subscriber count displays.

minor.issue: The rate-limit IP is the FIRST entry of X-Forwarded-For, which the client controls. The test sent a fake XFF header and the 5/hour limit was applied to that fake IP, so a bot can get past the limit by changing the header each time. Use the last entry added by the ingress, or the real client IP.
There is no TTL index, so the collection grows forever. Add a TTL index on 'at' (store it as a datetime) of about 1 hour.
Every platform vendor is included no matter its status (suspended or rejected vendors still get the digest). Vendors with empty business_categories get ALL tenders. Consider filtering by status.
The forced run ignores enabled=false and mode=instant. This is acceptable as a manual action, but say so in the UI.

issues: g.week.slice(0,8) drops the '-manual-HHMMSS' suffix, so manual and scheduled runs look identical. Show a 'manual' badge.
Long category names are cut off in the 3-column select row (e.g. 'Application implemen').
The 'How it works' heading shows 'contract,on' with no space after the comma at 390px.
